intro.headlineB: Interfaces that stay out of the way.
intro.lead: I’m {name}, a fullstack and backend developer in {location}. I design web applications that keep performing as users and features grow, and I still care about the last mile: the interface people actually touch.
intro.sceneLabel: Interactive 3D scene: the AD monogram on a pedestal, orbited by technology name plaques

work.title: Four habits you can check in the code.
work.subtitle: Claims are cheap. Each habit below points to something visible in this site’s repository.

backend.title: Backends that keep performing
backend.description: Scalable systems that stay fast, secure and reliable as users and features grow.
evidence: Container build with health checks (Docker Compose)
Production error tracking with Sentry since June 2025
Server-side rendering, plus a dynamic sitemap and robots for every locale

interfaces.title: Interfaces that stay accessible
interfaces.description: Clean, fast screens built on primitives that already handle focus, keyboard and screen readers.
evidence: Radix UI primitives behind each shadcn/ui component
One component tree serving English, Indonesian and German
Theme tokens with matching light and dark modes

content.title: Content kept apart from code
content.description: Editors change words and images in Sanity Studio; developers change behaviour in code. Neither blocks the other.
evidence: Typed content schemas for projects, skills, experience and more
Live preview and visual editing wired to the Studio
Server components fetch; client components only animate

teaching.title: Explains what it builds
teaching.description: Teaching forces clarity. I have been a lecturer assistant for web programming, basic programming and OOP.
evidence: Basic Programming and OOP lecturer assistant, 2024

architecture.title: This site, taken apart.
architecture.subtitle: From a client-rendered React app to a server-rendered, multilingual, CMS-driven site. Pick a node, in the scene or from the buttons, to see what it does.
architecture.sceneLabel: Interactive 3D diagram of this site’s architecture: Sanity, Spotify, Next.js, the browser, Vercel and Sentry, connected by animated data flows
architecture.fallback: Sanity → Next.js → Browser, hosted on Vercel, monitored by Sentry.
architecture.problem: The first portfolio was a client-rendered React app with its content written into components, and it spoke one language.
decisions: Render on the server, animate on the client
Move content into Sanity, behind typed schemas
Route by locale with next-intl: English, Indonesian, German
Track errors and keep a container path open

sanity.description: The single source of content. Server components query it with GROQ, filtered by language; draft mode and content source maps power live preview.

spotify.description: A route handler proxies the Spotify API, so the now-playing widget never exposes credentials to the browser.

next.description: App Router with server-side rendering. Locale routing through next-intl (English, Indonesian, German), a localized 404, and a dynamic sitemap and robots file.

browser.description: Client components handle motion and interaction with Framer Motion. Content arrives already rendered, so search engines and slow phones both get real HTML.

vercel.description: Deployed on Vercel with Analytics. A Dockerfile and a Compose file with health checks keep a self-hosted option open.

sentry.description: Errors from the server and the browser are reported to Sentry. It was wired in during June 2025, two months after the first commit.
